Three traps that catch White after 1.d4: the Englund, the Elephant and the Lasker. One wrong capture is all it takes. ♟️

ig_caption:
Play 1.d4? These three traps are waiting for you.

The Englund Gambit Trap ends in mate on c1. The Elephant Trap in the Queen's Gambit Declined turns a pawn grab into a lost piece. And the Lasker Trap in the Albin Countergambit finishes with a pawn promoting to a knight, with check.

Each one starts with a capture that looks free. Count the checks first.

Have you ever fallen for one of these? 👇

alt: Slide 1: Cover. Play 1.d4? Three traps to know. All three catch White. A chess diagram of the Englund Gambit Trap.
Slide 2: Englund Gambit Trap diagram. Black's queen checks, takes b2 and mates on c1 after White's 6.Bc3.
Slide 3: Elephant Trap diagram. White grabs on d5, Black gives the queen and wins it back with Bb4 check, ending a piece up.
Slide 4: Lasker Trap diagram. Black's pawn captures on f2 with check, then promotes to a knight on g1 with check.
Slide 5: A Chess Journey poster. The traps you fell for once are part of the climb too.

slides.title: Play 1.d4?
slides.moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Bc3 Bb4 Qd2 Bxc3 Qxc3 Qc1#

slides.title: Englund Gambit Trap
slides.moves: d4 e5 dxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Qe7 Bf4 Qb4+ Bd2 Qxb2 Bc3 Bb4 Qd2 Bxc3 Qxc3 Qc1#
slides.take: Black gives a pawn on move one. After 4.Bf4 the queen checks and takes b2, and 6.Bc3? walks into mate on c1.
slides.edge: The losing move is 6.Bc3?. When an enemy queen reaches b2, check what your rook and king have left undefended.

slides.title: Elephant Trap
slides.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7 cxd5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxd5 Bxd8 Bb4+ Qd2 Bxd2+ Kxd2 Kxd8
slides.take: 6.Nxd5? grabs a pawn because the f6 knight looks pinned. But 6...Nxd5! gives the queen, and 7...Bb4+ wins it back.
slides.edge: After the dust settles, Black is a piece up. A pin to a queen is not a pin to a king.
slides.movesText: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Nbd7 5.cxd5 exd5 6.Nxd5? Nxd5! 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ …

slides.title: Lasker Trap
slides.moves: d4 d5 c4 e5 dxe5 d4 e3 Bb4+ Bd2 dxe3 Bxb4 exf2+ Ke2 fxg1=N+
slides.take: 4.e3? lets Black's pawn run. After 6.Bxb4? it takes on f2 with check, then promotes to a knight, again with check.
slides.edge: Why a knight? A queen could be taken for free. The knight gives check, and after 8.Rxg1 Bg4+ wins White's queen.
